reviewNote: All photographs opened and visually inspected. Narration is fiction, not a documentary claim about the photographed individual. Parent must judge writing and image gates independently before acceptance. No text-only fallback. Independent review rejected 03 and 19 on prose. Entry 20 is withheld after its photograph moved to 14; 17 now uses the closed-mouth portrait formerly on 14. No full-batch acceptance is claimed.

entries.subject: river
entries.title: At ankle depth
entries.body:
They came in holding hands. At the first cold touch they both let go. I had expected to be the difficult part of this relationship.

One stayed on a stone while the other went deeper, making the small sharp noises people make when they discover that water has a temperature. The one on the stone laughed. Then stopped laughing, apparently remembering that they would have to come in eventually.

For a while there were two separate people, each trying to look less afraid than the other. Then a hand reached back. The second person took it and stepped down.

They stood together in my shallows, shivering. Neither looked triumphant. I liked them much better like that.

When they left, they each put on the wrong sandal.

image.alt: Bathers stand and wade in clear shallows between pale rocks
image.sceneMatch: Bathers stand and wade in clear shallows between pale rocks; the story builds on the awkward physical threshold into cold river water. Specific couple and sandal ending are invented narrative, not claimed documentation.

entries.subject: river
entries.title: A very slow disagreement
entries.body: The rock would like me to stop touching it. It has made this clear by remaining exactly where I touch it. I have tried both sides. This was taken as further touching.

image.alt: The river visibly separates around numerous large immovable boulders
image.sceneMatch: The river visibly separates around numerous large immovable boulders.

entries.payoff: A river's attempt to respect space is physically inseparable from renewed contact.

entries.subject: river
entries.title: The long way round
entries.body:
I split around the island this morning. On the left, I had a clear run. On the right, I caught in the gravel and spent a while turning a leaf in a circle.

The left side reached the other end first. Very pleased with itself. Then it had to wait for the rest of me, because I am a river and cannot abandon half my own sentence.

The delayed water arrived carrying the leaf. It had found a little stem to snag on, worked loose, been caught again, come free. Nothing important, unless you were the leaf.

Downstream, I spread into one current. The quick part took the leaf without asking.

I have been trying to work out which of me was impatient. Both sides keep pointing at the other bank.

image.alt: The photographed river divides around a tree-bearing rock island and rejoins
image.sceneMatch: The photographed river divides around a tree-bearing rock island and rejoins; this division is the actual story mechanism.

entries.subject: river
entries.title: I know every edge
entries.body: Here is the rock I have been smoothing. No, it is not finished. Yes, I have been at it for a while. There used to be a sharp bit here that caught everything I brought past. Now it is a little hollow. I keep bringing things past to feel it.

image.sceneMatch: Close view shows clear water pressed against sculpted pale stone and an undercut hollow, not generic distant scenery.

entries.subject: river
entries.title: Inside voice
entries.body:
The walls came close together and everybody said I sounded angry.

I was carrying the same water I had carried through the broad part. A little more hurried, yes. There were corners. There was a place where all of me wanted to pass at once, which is difficult when you have this much of yourself.

I struck the left wall, folded back, struck the right. Above me, the trees hardly moved. Very easy to be composed when nobody has asked you to fit through a crack.

Past the tightest turn I loosened into a pool. The noise fell away. A small bubble travelled across the surface, burst, and made the last objection.

I let it have that.

image.alt: Narrow pale rock gorge visibly constrains turbulent turquoise flow
image.sceneMatch: Narrow pale rock gorge visibly constrains turbulent turquoise flow; the central conflict is pressure and confinement.

entries.title: What I kept
entries.body: I tried to keep the mountain once. Held it whole on my surface: every pale ridge, even the bit of cloud it was wearing. Then the wind came and I lost it in a thousand places. The actual mountain was still there. I felt rather silly asking it to pose again.

entries.subject: soft shield fern
entries.title: Not yet
entries.body: I have been preparing to open for several days. Every time I get to the end of myself, there is another smaller me curled inside it. I had hoped to emerge mysterious. At this rate I shall emerge late.

image.alt: Detailed golden scaled fiddlehead contains nested curls
image.sceneMatch: Detailed golden scaled fiddlehead contains nested curls; focus-stack source is preserved.

entries.subject: soft shield fern
entries.title: The tall one
entries.body:
The tallest shoot came up first and immediately behaved as though the rest of me were an afterthought.

It had light. It had room. It unrolled a little farther every morning while the small one at the back stayed folded beside the stone. I resented it terribly. I was also the tall one, which made the resentment difficult to place.

For several days the little shoot barely changed. I kept making food in the bright part of myself. The small part kept using it. There was no satisfying way to withdraw my support without becoming less of a fern.

Then one morning there was a tiny green edge where the tight curl had been.

I spent the whole afternoon feeling pleased at the back and insufferable at the front.

image.alt: Whole crown of shoots at different heights beside rock provides the literal divided-body scene
image.sceneMatch: Whole crown of shoots at different heights beside rock provides the literal divided-body scene; six-image focus stack is retained.

entries.subject: soft shield fern
entries.title: Personal space
entries.body: A frond has been resting across me all morning. I waited politely. By noon I was furious. Followed it back to the base to see who thought this was acceptable. Me. Apparently I have been making myself uncomfortable for weeks and calling it a difficult neighbor.

image.alt: Clearly overlapping green fronds give the physical cause
image.sceneMatch: Clearly overlapping green fronds give the physical cause; no animal visitor is fabricated.

entries.subject: soft shield fern
entries.title: Underneath
entries.body:
A person lifted my frond and turned it over.

I had spent the season making a perfectly respectable green surface. Fine edges. Orderly divisions. Nothing ostentatious. They looked at that for a moment, then went straight underneath.

There were all my brown little spore clusters, in rows. The part of me that had been getting on with reproduction while the top tried to look serene.

The person leaned closer. I could have endured a quick glance. They brought another person.

I remained, of course, a fern. There are limits to what indignation can accomplish without legs. After they left, the frond settled back into place.

I have since put a little more effort into the green surface. I refuse to become known solely for what I do underneath.

entries.subject: soft shield fern
entries.title: Lost count
entries.body: I tried to count all the little parts of my leaf. Reached a convincing number. Discovered a row underneath. Started again. By sunset I had stopped knowing whether I was counting myself or growing additional objections.

entries.subject: soft shield fern
entries.title: A small gap
entries.body: One of my leaflets is shorter than the others. I kept expecting it to catch up. Now the frond is grown and there it is, still short, with a little more sky beside it. I had a whole complaint ready. A spot of sunlight got through and warmed the bit of me underneath. I've kept the complaint. Just not sent it.

entries.subject: mugger crocodile
entries.title: Armored
entries.body: As a young crocodile I thought the armor meant I would stop feeling things. Then I lay on these stones. There is one directly under the soft part of my belly. I have shifted three times. The stone has not moved and is winning the argument without any armor at all.

image.alt: Crocodile lies over conspicuously uneven reddish stones with belly pressed down
image.sceneMatch: Crocodile lies over conspicuously uneven reddish stones with belly pressed down; no prey or attack.

entries.subject: mugger crocodile
entries.title: Nothing to discuss
entries.body:
I said I wanted the bank to myself. The other crocodile went into the water.

For a while it was excellent. No tail where my tail should be. No slow scraping sound. No eye opening whenever I moved, as if I were planning something.

Then the sun reached the patch where he usually lay. It warmed beautifully. I did not move into it. I had already arranged myself, and getting up would have been a great deal of unnecessary crocodile.

He came back later. Stopped at the edge of the bank. I kept my eye shut.

After a while there was the scraping sound. His tail came to rest near mine. It was not quite touching.

I moved mine the last small distance. The bank slopes there. That's all.

image.alt: Two mugger crocodiles share a low basking island with softshell turtles
image.sceneMatch: Two crocodiles visibly share the small bank. Their return and voluntary tail contact are fictional events; the photo supports close companionship but does not resolve tail contact.

entries.subject: mugger crocodile
entries.title: Open
entries.body: The little animals keep interpreting my open mouth as a statement. I am hot. That is the entire statement. They retreat, I get a breeze, and somehow this has become a very effective way to maintain friendships.

entries.subject: mugger crocodile
entries.title: The departure
entries.body: I meant to leave with finality. Lifted the front. Lifted the middle. Stood there for a moment. I had put rather more effort into getting up than into deciding where to go.

entries.subject: mugger crocodile
entries.title: You can come closer
entries.body: I tried to make my face less alarming. Closed my mouth. Several teeth remained outside. Nobody had mentioned this to me. I have been attempting reassurance with exposed teeth for years.

image.alt: Mugger crocodile resting with its mouth closed and several teeth still visible

entries.subject: mugger crocodile
entries.title: Do not interrupt
entries.body:
I closed my eye because the morning had become crowded. Birds crossing. Water flashing. Something small making a determined noise in the grass.

Darkness was better. Warmth on my face, cool earth underneath, nothing I needed to turn toward. I was almost free of the whole business of having an opinion.

Then the sun went behind a cloud.

I waited for it to return. Waited a little longer. Opened my eye to check whether it understood the inconvenience. Of course the cloud continued. Clouds can afford to be indifferent. They are not lying here trying to digest.

When the warmth came back I shut my eye again. I had achieved peace, apart from keeping track of the cloud.

image.alt: Crocodile explicitly photographed with closed eye and mouth open in sun
image.sceneMatch: Crocodile explicitly photographed with closed eye and mouth open in sun; the remembered cloud explains the limits of its withdrawal.

entries.subject: mugger crocodile
entries.title: Most of me
entries.body: Back in the water. The heavy parts stopped insisting on themselves. For a moment I forgot my own weight. Then my tail brushed something and I remembered how far away the end of me is. I checked on it. Still mine.

image.alt: Aerial photograph of swimming mugger in green water shows entire long body supported by water
image.sceneMatch: Aerial photograph of swimming mugger in green water shows entire long body supported by water.

entries.subject: mugger crocodile
entries.title: The warm patch
entries.body:
The turtles arrived first. By the time I came out, there was no good space left on the island. Just the edge, beside them.

I lay there with my mouth open. This generally communicates enough. A turtle adjusted its neck and continued being warm. Another was angled toward the sun with the absolute confidence of something that brings its own roof.

I could have gone to the empty bank. I could see it from here. Plenty of space. No shells. No one breathing nearby.

Instead I stayed. The other crocodile stayed too. We became a small, badly arranged collection of backs.

Later a turtle shifted. A little sunlight reached the side of my jaw.

I moved into it very slowly, so nobody would mistake this for gratitude.
entries.payoff: A supposedly antisocial predator chooses crowded company, then disguises pleasure as thermoregulation.
